text:
liam: FYI bringing up atlas-triton-48k int3 on long fuzzbench. Hitting reproducible phase-drift after ~42k tokens that causes KV-shard mismatch and occasional decode token flips.
nora: can you share the repro flags?
liam: ./ci/run_onboard.sh --model atlas-triton-48k --quant int3 --seq 45000 --batch 1 --seed 7 --mode long-fuzz
bench-bot: run_id=1807774444, config={quant:int3,rope:scaled_dynamic,evict:async,shards:4}
liam: log snippet:
```
[kv_write] shard=2 write_pos=42198 expected_checksum=0x7af8 got=0x7ae9
[kv_read] shard=2 read_pos=42198 returned_chunk_id=42199
[token] output: "and" -> then "\t" at pos 42204
[perf] tok_latency: 142ms -> 176ms
```
pavan: that read_pos off-by-one plus checksum delta looks like a race or pointer arithmetic flub when we quantize indices to int16. int3 path uses packed indexing and a small accumulator.
nora: does fp16 path reproduce?
liam: ran fp16 and int8-uniform — both clean to 45k. int3-only.
pavan: suspect compacted-packed-write in kv_shard_writer. If a partial vector write gets shifted by one byte, subsequent reads shift by token.
nora: try setting SHARD_WRITE_ATOMIC=1 and KV_PREFETCH=0 — see if it avoids tearing.
liam: quick patch: SHARD_WRITE_ATOMIC=1 KV_PREFETCH=0 -> drift moves to ~43.5k instead of 42.1k, still repro.
triage-bot: Incident IN-180777-KV-DRIFT created and assigned to eng-ml.
ops-bot: snapshot saved: s3://redwood-ci/onboard/atlas-triton/1807774444/snap.tar.gz
liam: I added extra checksums in kv_writer and kv_reader. Checksum diff spikes right before the write that toggles. Looks like phase-to-index mapping diverges after a rounding event in rotary interpolation.
pavan: can you dump the rotary phase table around those positions and the quantized LUT?
liam: dumped files attached to snapshot: /diagnostics/rotary_phase_42000-42500.csv and /diagnostics/rot_lut_int3.csv
ora: idea: perform periodic phase re-eval at hard boundaries (every 2k tokens) and compare with incremental accumulation. If re-eval != accumulated, force re-eval to writer.
pavan: try toggling ROTARY_REEVAL_INTERVAL=2000 and run with cheaper checksum validation first. If it reduces divergence, we know accumulation is drifting.
liam: ran with ROTARY_REEVAL_INTERVAL=2000: drift still shows but checksum delta smaller and token flip delayed to ~44.2k. So accumulation contributes but isn't entire cause.
ora: maybe both accumulation rounding and partial-shard writes combine — one pushes index slightly and the other allows a shifted write to persist.
liam: running micro-bisect: switch int3 kernel impl from packed->unaligned-write to conservative vector write.
liam: conservative write run: no drift up to 50k (trial 1). Rolling more runs now.
nora: if conservative write helps, we can land a hotfix to fallback on risky kernels for long-context runs until a full kernel fix.
triage-bot: next steps assigned: pavan (kernel audit + add safe path), nora (eviction/prefetch matrix), liam (full-run logs + attach checksums), bench-bot (automate long-run smoke for int3).
liam: will also add a lightweight phase checksum emitted every 500 tokens to the production-int3 path behind a flag DEBUG_PHASE_CHECK=1. Keep it cheap.
pavan: noted. I'll prototype a small patch that avoids byte-shift by aligning packed writes and adding an expicit write-barrier.
nora: thanks. also add a small perf guard so we can opt into conservative writes only for long sequences or when DEBUG_PHASE_CHECK sees drift.
liam: closing loop: fp16/int8 clean, int3 repro. Conservative write eliminates repro in initial trials. Will open PR with safe fallback and perf guard.
liam: posting PR link when ready. Thanks team. :ok_hand:
